rationale: C03 has the closest phrasing, pairing the recipient's leadership position and broad experience with a request for additional service, but this is generic appointment-letter language and does not reproduce the child's ex officio liaison arrangement. C07 and C06 concern the same highway-safety program and related coordination needs, yet neither contains the distinctive administrative mechanism of asking an Advisory Council chairman to join a separate Committee ex officio to strengthen liaison between the two bodies. The similarities therefore reflect shared subject matter and routine presidential correspondence rather than a concrete, material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I should like to ask you, as Chairman of the Advisory Council, to serve also as an ex officio member of the Committee.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: As the President of the Federal City Council, and with your broad experiences in civic affairs, I am certain you can render a service of great value.
shared_material.explanation: C03 shares the formulation of invoking an existing leadership position and broad experience when requesting service, but lacks the ex officio appointment and inter-body liaison machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: turning your interest and broad experience in traffic problems to the urgent traffic safety program
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I should like to have you spearhead a renewed highway safety program and serve as General Chairman of the President's Highway Safety Conference.
shared_material.explanation: C07 shares the highway-safety subject and a request to assume a chairmanship, but its operative assignment is materially different.

shared_material.child_excerpt: contribute significantly to strengthened Committee liaison with the national highway safety organizations represented on the Advisory Council
shared_material.parent_excerpt: to promote effective cooperation among Federal, State and local agencies
shared_material.explanation: C06 similarly emphasizes coordination in a committee setting, but only at a broad functional level and in an unrelated narcotics program.
